title: UPSClear
question: How does an inverter or UPS work?
hook: When the power cuts out and the fans keep turning, a box in the corner is quietly turning a battery's DC back into 230 V AC. Take a home inverter and a computer UPS apart in 3D, and watch the switch happen in milliseconds.

explainer.title: Store it now, give it back later
explainer.text: A home inverter is a battery, a charger and an inverter in one box. While the mains is on it fills a 12 V battery; in a power cut it turns that battery's energy back into 230 V AC for your fans and lights. A computer UPS is the same idea, shrunk down.

explainer.title: AC into DC: four diodes and a capacitor
explainer.text: Mains in India swings between +325 V and −325 V fifty times a second. A transformer steps it down, a bridge of four diodes flips the backwards half of each wave, and a capacitor smooths the bumps. The charger then fills the battery in stages: bulk, about 14.4 V absorption, then about 13.5 V float.

explainer.title: DC into AC: four switches and a transformer
explainer.text: Four MOSFET switches in an H-bridge connect the battery one way round, then the other, 50 times a second. Pure sine inverters switch thousands of times a second in pulses of changing width and filter them smooth. A transformer with about 19 times more turns lifts 12 V to 230 V, and the current drops by the same factor.

explainer.title: Switching over in milliseconds
explainer.text: An offline UPS lets mains straight through and clicks a relay over to its inverter when the mains fails, in about 5 to 15 ms. A PC survives the gap on the capacitor inside its power supply. An online UPS runs from its inverter all the time, so there is no gap at all.

explainer.title: How long the backup lasts
explainer.text: 12 V × 150 Ah is 1,800 Wh, but only about 80% is usable, the inverter loses about 15%, and draining a battery fast gives less capacity (Peukert's law). Two ordinary fans, four LED bulbs, a TV and a router run for about three and a half hours; with BLDC fans, nearly six.

explainer.title: Inside the battery
explainer.text: Six lead-acid cells of about 2.1 V make 12.6 V. Discharging turns both plates into lead sulfate and weakens the acid, so a hydrometer reading shows the charge. Charging splits a little water, so it needs distilled water topped up. LiFePO₄ batteries use four 3.2 V cells, weigh about a third as much and last thousands of cycles.

concepts.def: Alternating current keeps reversing, 50 times a second in India; direct current flows one way, like a battery's.
A circuit, usually four diodes in a bridge, that turns AC into current flowing one way.
A circuit that turns DC into AC by switching a battery's connection back and forth.
Four switches that can connect a load either way round to a battery.
Pulse-width modulation: fast on-off pulses whose changing widths average out to a smooth wave.
Two coils on an iron core that step AC voltage up or down; the current changes the other way.
The gap between the mains failing and the backup taking over: about 10 ms for an offline UPS, zero for an online one.
How much charge a battery holds. Volts × amp-hours gives the energy in watt-hours.
The density of a lead-acid battery's acid compared with water: about 1.26 when full, 1.12 when flat.
